# CC04: 思永斋 Siyong Zhai

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC04` · Page: `/scenes/#CC04` · Row: `research/buildings/CC04-siyong-zhai/`

## What it was

思永斋 Siyong Zhai, "Studio of Long Reflection", stood north of the stream behind 蒨园: a seven-bay hall, gate plaque 静便趣 and inner plaque 萬横香玉, with the tower 山色湖光共一楼 over the water to the north and the side court 小有天园 to the east (S05 j83:9a-9b; E0135). Begun 1747 on a ringed island (E0138). Qianlong wrote in 1785 that it had stood over twenty years, older than 宁寿宫, and like it was meant for his retirement (E0136). The east court copies 小有天园, the 汪 family garden at 南屏, Hangzhou, named on the tour of 1751 and seen again in 1757: rockwork as 慧日峰, a tin-roofed room, a cascade and small Huangshan pines (S05 j83:9b-10b, E0134; Malone E0137). S361 adds an octagonal gallery to the tower and copies of the recut 淳化阁帖 and of the 西洋楼 engravings kept inside (E0138). Poems run to 1831 (E0136). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 乾隆十二年 1747 基本建成 (S43); by 1758; had stood 'over twenty years' by 1785; 小有天園 court: after 丁丑 1757 (記); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S43, S01, S201, S361).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Nothing written yet.

### The garden around it

小有天园: in a room ten 笏 square with a window half that, rocks piled as a peak (慧日), a room roofed in tin (範錫為宇), a cascade, Huangshan pines among stone shoots (S05 j83:9b-10b: 範錫為宇又依然壑庵也 ... 激水作瀑). Blue-and-white tiles from 思永斋 were among the restored dig finds of 2019 (E1339), so some walls or floors were faced in porcelain tile.

## What survives today

Ruin photographs of 2013 show the hall site, the 小有天园 court and a fish pond (P0411, P0412, P0445, P0446). Blue-and-white tiles from the site are in the park's restoration programme (E1339). No dig report found.

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.
